mind_map.root_node: Travelling, Now and Then (5-Digit Numbers & Historical Travel)

key_nodes: Ten Thousands (TTh), Thousands (Th), Hundreds (H), Tens (T), Ones (O)
10 Thousand = 10,000 (5-digit baseline)
sub_branches.misconception_alert: Confusing face value of a digit with its place value (e.g., in 74,520, place value of 7 is 70,000).

key_nodes: Expanded form notation (e.g., 58,042 = 50,000 + 8,000 + 40 + 2)
Predecessor (-1) and Successor (+1)
Comparing and ordering 5-digit numbers column by column
sub_branches.rule_or_formula: To compare 5-digit numbers, compare digits from left (Ten Thousands) to right.

key_nodes: Nearest Tens: look at ones digit
Nearest Hundreds: look at tens digit
Nearest Thousands: look at hundreds digit
sub_branches.real_world_application: Estimating travel costs, total journey distances, and fuel expenses.

key_nodes: Odometer tracking (Final Reading - Initial Reading = Distance Traveled)
Speed-Distance-Time relationships in road trips
sub_branches.formula_or_rule: Distance = Speed x Time; Speed = Distance / Time

key_nodes: Numerator (top): Number of equal parts taken
Denominator (bottom): Total equal parts into which the whole is divided
Unit Fraction: Numerator is 1 (e.g., 1/2, 1/3, 1/4)
sub_branches.misconception_alert: Assuming larger denominator always means larger fraction (e.g., 1/8 is smaller than 1/4).

key_nodes: Proper Fraction: Numerator < Denominator (e.g., 3/5)
Improper Fraction: Numerator >= Denominator (e.g., 7/4)
Fractions Greater Than 1 & Mixed Numbers (e.g., 1 3/4)
sub_branches.formula_or_rule: Same Whole Rule: Fractional parts can only be compared if derived from identical whole sizes.

key_nodes: Generating equivalent fractions by multiplying/dividing numerator and denominator by same non-zero number
Fraction Strip Kits for visual comparison (e.g., two 1/8 strips = one 1/4 strip)
Equal sharing of foods (pizzas, parathas) among groups
sub_branches.real_world_application: Dividing food portions fairly and calculating recipe ingredient shares.

key_nodes: Right Angle: Exactly 90° (Quarter Turn / 'L' shape corner)
Acute Angle: Less than 90° (Sharp turn)
Obtuse Angle: Between 90° and 180° (Wide turn)
Straight Angle: Exactly 180° (Half Turn / Straight line)
sub_branches.misconception_alert: Thinking angle size depends on arm length rather than degree of opening.

key_nodes: 1 Full Turn = 360°
Clock positions: 3:00 forms 90°, 6:00 forms 180°, 1:00 forms 30°
sub_branches.formula_or_rule: Each hour mark on a 12-hour clock face represents 30° (360° / 12 = 30°).

key_nodes: Clockwise vs Anti-clockwise rotations
Cardinal directions: North, South, East, West
90° clockwise turn from North faces East; 180° turn faces opposite direction
sub_branches.real_world_application: Yoga postures, gymnastics, compass navigation, and crane boom turns.

mind_map.root_node: We the Travellers — II (Large Number Arithmetic & Patterns)

key_nodes: Column alignment by place value (TTh, Th, H, T, O)
Addition with carrying / regrouping across place values
Subtraction with borrowing across zeroes
sub_branches.formula_or_rule: Inverse Relationship: Minuend - Subtrahend = Difference; Difference + Subtrahend = Minuend.

key_nodes: Palindromic numbers read the same forward and backward (e.g., 121, 4554)
Reverse-and-add method to generate palindromes
Sums of consecutive natural numbers
sub_branches.misconception_alert: Assuming all reversed additions immediately yield a palindrome in one step.

key_nodes: Total travel distance calculations across multi-city routes
Fuel consumption and budget balancing
Round-trip distance estimation
sub_branches.real_world_application: Planning road trips, fuel stop budgets, and tracking highway tolls.

mind_map.root_node: Far and Near (Metric Length Units & Conversions)

key_nodes: Millimetre (mm): Micro measurements (e.g., coin thickness)
Centimetre (cm): Short objects (e.g., pencil, book)
Metre (m): Room dimensions, cloth, track lengths
Kilometre (km): Long distances between towns and cities
Larger to smaller unit: Multiply by conversion factor (e.g., 3.5 km = 3,500 m)
Smaller to larger unit: Divide by conversion factor (e.g., 250 cm = 2.5 m)
Double Number Lines for visual proportional scale mapping
sub_branches.misconception_alert: Multiplying instead of dividing when converting smaller units to larger units.

key_nodes: Addition & Subtraction of compound lengths (m and cm, km and m)
Map Scale Translations (e.g., 1 cm on map = 10 km on ground)
Fabric requirements and per-metre cost calculations
sub_branches.real_world_application: Tailoring cloth cuts, athletic race track measurements, and road map scale reading.

key_nodes: Appending zeroes rule (e.g., 45 x 10 = 450; 32 x 100 = 3,200)
Multiplication by zero yields 0; multiplication by 1 preserves value
Halving and Doubling strategy (e.g., 14 x 5 -> 7 x 10 = 70)
sub_branches.formula_or_rule: Distributive Law: a x (b + c) = (a x b) + (a x c).

key_nodes: Decomposing 2-digit numbers into tens and ones (e.g., 23 x 12 = (20+3)x(10+2))
Grid Area Model mapping spatial products
Summing partial products to reach total product
sub_branches.misconception_alert: Forgetting to add all four partial product terms in grid multiplication.

key_nodes: Daily milk yield calculations across herds
Revenue and pricing calculations per litre
Auditorium seating grid problems and compost pit area models
sub_branches.real_world_application: Managing dairy cooperative sales, egg crate packing, and daily wage payouts.

key_nodes: Tessellation: Covering a surface completely without gaps or overlaps
Shapes that tessellate: Squares, rectangles, regular hexagons, equilateral triangles
Non-tessellating shapes: Circles, regular pentagons, irregular curved shapes
sub_branches.misconception_alert: Believing all regular polygons tessellate seamlessly on a flat plane.

key_nodes: Triangle classification: Equilateral (3 equal sides), Isosceles (2 equal sides), Scalene (0 equal sides)
Quadrilaterals: Square, Rectangle, Rhombus, Parallelogram, Trapezium
Polygons by side count: Pentagon (5), Hexagon (6), Octagon (8)
7-Piece Tangram Puzzle geometry
sub_branches.formula_or_rule: Polygon: A closed 2D shape composed entirely of straight line segments.

key_nodes: Cube Net: 6 square faces unfolding into flat pattern
Cube properties: 6 Faces, 8 Vertices, 12 Edges
Regular Dodecahedron (12 pentagonal faces) & Icosahedron (20 triangular faces)
sub_branches.formula_or_rule: Euler's Polyhedron Formula: Faces (F) + Vertices (V) - Edges (E) = 2.

mind_map.root_node: Weight and Capacity (Mass, Volume & Unit Metrics)

key_nodes: Milligram (mg): Tiny active pharmaceutical doses
Gram (g): Kitchen ingredients, butter, paper
Kilogram (kg): Vegetables, human body weight, groceries
Quintal (100 kg) & Tonne (1,000 kg): Commercial bulk harvest loads
sub_branches.formula_or_rule: 1 g = 1,000 mg; 1 kg = 1,000 g; 1 Quintal = 100 kg; 1 Tonne = 1,000 kg.

key_nodes: Millilitre (ml): Liquid medicine doses, juice pouches, spoons
Litre (l): Water bottles, milk buckets, fuel tanks
Pan Balance Equilibrium: Left Mass = Right Mass
Fractional weights: 1/2 kg = 500 g; 3/4 kg = 750 g; 1/4 l = 250 ml
Double Number Lines for weight-capacity mapping
sub_branches.real_world_application: Baking recipes, dairy packaging, and agricultural grain market sales.

key_nodes: Dividend: Total quantity being divided
Divisor: Number of equal groups or group size
Quotient: Resulting count per group
Remainder: Unassigned left-over amount
sub_branches.formula_or_rule: Fundamental Division Identity: Dividend = (Divisor x Quotient) + Remainder, where 0 <= Remainder < Divisor.

key_nodes: Partial Quotients Method: Subtracting easy multiples (10s, 20s, 50s)
Zero placement in quotient when dividend digit < divisor (e.g., 612 / 6 = 102)
Division by 10s and 100s place-value shortcuts
sub_branches.misconception_alert: Forgetting to record zero in the quotient when bringing down a digit that cannot be divided.

key_nodes: Coconut bag packaging in fixed counts
Oil extraction ratio calculations (e.g., 10 coconuts = 1 litre oil)
Dividing harvest earnings equally among farm workers
sub_branches.real_world_application: Packaging copra sacks, calculating yield per tree, and sharing farm profits.

key_nodes: Line of Symmetry: Axis dividing figure into identical mirror halves
Square: 4 lines of symmetry
Rectangle: 2 lines of symmetry
Equilateral Triangle: 3 lines; Regular Hexagon: 6 lines; Circle: Infinite lines
sub_branches.misconception_alert: Thinking diagonal of a non-square rectangle is a line of symmetry.

key_nodes: Rotational Symmetry: Shape looks identical after rotation less than 360°
1/4 Turn (90°) Rotational Symmetry: Square, 4-blade firki windmill
1/2 Turn (180°) Rotational Symmetry: Rectangle, letters H, I, N, O, S, X, Z
sub_branches.formula_or_rule: Order of Rotational Symmetry: Number of times shape matches original position during 360° turn.

key_nodes: Rajasthani block printing repeated motifs
Paper firkis (windmills) and folded paper cut-outs
Symmetry in nature (butterfly wings, human face, flower petals)
sub_branches.real_world_application: Textile block printing, architectural tile motifs, and logo design.

key_nodes: Perimeter: Total boundary length surrounding a 2D closed figure
Perimeter of Rectangle = 2 x (Length + Breadth)
Perimeter of Square = 4 x Side
Unit of measurement: Linear units (cm, m, km)
sub_branches.formula_or_rule: Perimeter = Sum of all outer boundary side lengths.

key_nodes: Area: Total surface region enclosed within 2D boundary
Area of Rectangle = Length x Breadth
Area of Square = Side x Side (Side²)
Unit of measurement: Square units (sq cm, sq m)
sub_branches.misconception_alert: Confusing linear perimeter units (m) with square area units (sq m).

key_nodes: Counting full, half, and greater-than-half unit squares on grid paper
Shapes with same area can have different perimeters (e.g., 1x12 vs 3x4 rectangles)
Area Optimization: Square shape maximizes area for a fixed perimeter length
sub_branches.real_world_application: Quilt patchwork design, room floor tiling, garden fencing, and tablecloth lace trimming.

key_nodes: 1 Minute = 60 Seconds
1 Hour = 60 Minutes = 3,600 Seconds
Fractional conversions: 1/2 min = 30 sec; 1/4 min = 15 sec
Convert minutes to seconds: Multiply by 60; seconds to minutes: Divide by 60
sub_branches.formula_or_rule: Base-60 System: Time units scale by multiples of 60.

key_nodes: 12-Hour Clock: Uses AM (Midnight to Noon) and PM (Noon to Midnight)
24-Hour Clock: 00:00 (Midnight), 12:00 (Noon), 14:30 (2:30 PM)
PM to 24-Hour conversion: Add 12 to hour digit
sub_branches.misconception_alert: Adding 12 to morning AM hours when converting to 24-hour time.

key_nodes: Elapsed Time = End Time - Start Time
Digital stopwatches measuring split seconds (hundredths of a second)
Adding and subtracting compound time durations (hours, minutes, seconds)
sub_branches.real_world_application: Athletic track sprint timing, railway timetable reading, and daily schedule planning.

key_nodes: Multiple: Product of a number and any whole number (e.g., Multiples of 3: 3, 6, 9, 12...)
Common Multiples: Shared landing numbers on jump grid
Least Common Multiple (LCM): First shared landing spot
sub_branches.formula_or_rule: Multiples of a number are infinite.

key_nodes: Factor: Whole number dividing given number completely with zero remainder
Prime Number: Exactly 2 factors (1 and itself; e.g., 2, 3, 5, 7, 11)
Composite Number: More than 2 factors (e.g., 4, 6, 8, 9, 10)
Number 1: Neither prime nor composite
sub_branches.misconception_alert: Thinking all odd numbers are prime (e.g., 9 and 15 are odd but composite).

key_nodes: Divisibility by 2: Ends in even digit (0, 2, 4, 6, 8)
Divisibility by 5: Ends in 0 or 5
Divisibility by 10: Ends in 0
Divisibility by 3: Sum of digits is divisible by 3
sub_branches.real_world_application: Grouping objects into equal rows, tile arrangement, and rhythm leap games.

mind_map.root_node: Maps and Locations (Spatial Orientation & Grid Coordinates)

key_nodes: Primary Cardinal Directions: North (top), South (bottom), East (right), West (left)
Sun orientation: Rises in East, sets in West
Magnetic compass needle pointing to magnetic North
Coordinate Pair (x, y): x = Horizontal column, y = Vertical row
Origin Point: (0, 0)
Taxicab Grid Distance: Sum of horizontal and vertical block movements
sub_branches.misconception_alert: Reversing horizontal (x) and vertical (y) coordinates when plotting points.

key_nodes: Map Legend / Key: Decoding color lines, markers, and symbols
Scale Translation: Reducing large ground distances to paper scale (e.g., 1 cm = 5 km)
Delhi Metro network map route tracing
sub_branches.real_world_application: Navigating city transit routes, bird migration path tracking, and architectural floor plan reading.

mind_map.root_node: Data Through Pictures (Data Handling & Visual Analytics)

key_nodes: Primary Data: Firsthand information gathered via counting or measurement
Tally Marks: Vertical strokes grouped in 5-line bundles (卌 = 5)
Frequency Tables: Summarizing raw counts into organized category rows
sub_branches.formula_or_rule: Every 5th tally mark is drawn diagonally across 4 vertical strokes.

key_nodes: Pictograph: Using icons/pictures to represent quantitative values
Scaled Key: Assigning value to each symbol (e.g., 1 tree icon = 10 trees)
Partial Symbols: Representing fractions of key value (e.g., half icon = 5 trees)
sub_branches.misconception_alert: Misinterpreting total quantity by counting symbols without multiplying by key value.

key_nodes: Bar Graph Axes: Horizontal X-axis (Categories), Vertical Y-axis (Value Scale)
Bar height/length directly proportional to category frequency
Comparing categories, finding mode (most frequent item), and total sums
sub_branches.real_world_application: Tracking canteen food wastage, analyzing attendance records, and reporting survey findings.
